role_note: The original host this suite was built for (Dr. Ben Winters). Here he is a voice reference: transcripts of 103 of his real videos (66 long, 37 Shorts, about 228,000 words, mostly unscripted) show what natural spoken rhythm looks like next to a written script. Borrow rhythm (how sentences start, run on, hedge and turn to 'you'); never his catchphrases, persona, profession or claims. Never a swipe-research target. His rules (docs/ben-rules.md) and house voice (docs/style-prompts/bentist-measured.md) are worked examples of what the new host's files should look like.
name: TheBentist
host: Dr. Ben Winters, orthodontist in Plano, Texas
niche: orthodontics and dental reactions (Orthodontist Reacts, myth vs truth, dental explainers)
audience: Teens, young adults and parents: braces wearers, people anxious about the dentist, people who love watching a real doctor react to wild dental content
market: United States first, then English-speaking worldwide
editing_styles_note: reaction = clip reactions (blend of Ben's two reaction videos + SSSniperWolf; styles/reaction-1 is Ben's faster one, reaction-2 his calmer one). story = Huge If True-style storytelling (Cleo Abram). explainer = Vsauce-style, not learned yet (the download was blocked). editing_style is the fallback.
transcribe_prompt: Hi, I'm Dr. Ben Winters, an orthodontist. Um, so today we're talking about braces, Invisalign, cavities, Strep mutans, P. gingivalis, and your oral microbiome. Okay? Let's get into it.
script_wpm_note: Learned from the bad-breath read, 2026-09-28: script words per finished (silence-cut) minute when Ben records a script. He says 1.34 words per script word and speaks script content at 188 wpm after silence cuts (230 when riffing, = fingerprint median), so 2,543 script words ran 18:09. The default --wpm for retention-check.mjs and read-copy.mjs. Evidence: videos/bad-breath-for-good/take/read-lessons.md
